proposed.sourceName: IFANCA — The Halal Gelatin Story (M. Munir Chaudry, Ph.D.)
proposed.paraphrase: IFANCA recounts rejecting certificates for cattle-bone gelatin once it was clear the cattle were not slaughtered by Muslims, and requires cattle to be slaughtered by Muslims reciting Tasmiyyah and Takbir; gelatin from non-Islamically-slaughtered animals is therefore not certified halal.

proposed.sourceName: Heliyon — Towards halal pharmaceutical: Exploring alternatives to animal-based ingredients (Herdiana et al.)
proposed.paraphrase: Peer-reviewed review stating gelatin is collagen-derived from pig and bovine tissue and that halal certification is essential for gelatin from non-halal animals; non-halal-slaughtered animal gelatin is not permissible absent halal certification.

researcherNote: Lenient (most permissive synthesized) position. A MINORITY of scholars permit non-zabiha gelatin via istihalah (complete chemical transformation), but the dominant authorities (IFANCA, JAKIM, MUI, HMC, European Council for Fatwa) reject it, so it remains 'widely avoided' even under a lenient lens -> seeded draft grade 4. Lenient requires two independent sources; IFANCA standard body + Heliyon peer-reviewed present. The istihalah divergence is surfaced in the contested appendix. APPROVED by owner 2026-06-28.
